editorial_reason: The nonempty/proper and no-greatest-element conditions are all essential for representing finite real numbers uniquely. The upward-cut and (lower,upper)-partition conventions are equivalent presentations only after a consistent endpoint convention is chosen.

The representation q↦{r∈Q:r<q} is injective and order-preserving. Under strict lower-cut convention equality of real numbers is literal equality of cuts; abstract real field systems are isomorphic, not literally this set. Do not assert field/completeness without the separate proofs of operations.

Nonemptiness makes the union nonempty. An upper bound B≠Q ensures the union is proper. Downward closure and the no-greatest-element condition pass to the union, so it is a cut and is the least upper bound by inclusion. The hypothesis S bounded above is required. This is not the definition of generic Dedekind completeness of any ordered set.

Only the rational order, arithmetic, and absolute value appear in this definition; no real limit is assumed. Do not identify a Cauchy rational sequence with a rational limit because some lack one in Q.

The difference a_n−b_n tends to zero in the already defined rational convergence sense. Reflexivity and symmetry are immediate; transitivity follows from the triangle inequality after splitting ε into halves. 'Same real limit' cannot serve as the definition because real numbers are not yet constructed.

Arithmetic definitions must be shown independent of representative; this uses boundedness of Cauchy sequences and ε-arguments. A compatible total order must be built on classes, and Cauchy completeness and equivalence with least-upper-bound completeness need proofs. Do not define positivity of a class merely by eventually positive representatives: (1/n) represents zero.

The eventual positive margin δ, not merely pointwise positivity or eventual a_n>0, is necessary. A rational Cauchy sequence such as 1/n is positive in every term but belongs to the zero equivalence class. Representative independence follows by choosing ε=δ/2. The sum/product closure and trichotomy of resulting classes are separate results.
